mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which may accelerate inflation and prompt further rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% and UNRATE decline exceeds 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle economic expansion, declining housing starts (HOUST) and slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) signal an impending slowdown, prompting the Fed to cut rates and generate positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 growth is below 2% and HOUST growth is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes economic slowdowns and Fed rate cuts, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO growth is negative.

mechanism_narrative: High year-over-year inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5%) signals persistent inflationary pressures, leading the Federal Reserve to maintain high interest rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5% YoY) indicate a tightening monetary cycle, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.2% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 5%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.2% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) indicates a tight labor market, which may fuel wage inflation and accelerate Federal Reserve rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE is below 3.5%.
